tagline.text: An all-in-one beach resort on the Dapitan coast, open since 1988

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Taguilon, Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte

children.text: Dakak Park and Beach Resort is a large beach resort that opened in 1988 on the coast of Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte. It packs a long white-sand beach, swimming pools, water sports and a golf course into one property, and it sits close to the places where José Rizal lived in exile.
The name Dakak is said to come from the Visayan phrase dakong kakahoyan, meaning "big forest." The site began as a roughly
15-hectare

beachfront estate originally meant for housing in the 1980s, and in 1988 it was turned into a leisure resort that is still running today. It is one of the best-known beach resorts in the southern Philippines.
The resort stands along the coastal road in Barangay Taguilon, Dapitan City. It has a white-sand beach about

long, three swimming pools of different sizes and depths, and about 160 rooms in total. A forested hillside rises behind the beach, so once you check in you can eat, play and relax without leaving the grounds.

The main facilities include a water sports center (kayaking, paddleboarding, jet skis, parasailing and PADI Discover Scuba Diving), land activities such as horseback riding and ATVs, a separate golf club, yoga programs, and the upscale annex Villa Angelina Luxury Suites. Which of these are running at any given moment changes over time, so please confirm before you book.
There is more to the trip than the resort. Dapitan is where José Rizal lived in exile for four years, from 1892 to 1896. The Rizal Park and Rizal Shrine lie about
3.8 km

from the resort, so you can spend one day on the beach and another visiting the historic sites. On May 7, 2026, the owning family announced that it had handed operations to a new entity, so it is safest to check facilities and rates against the new management's current information.

blocks.title: 750 m of white sand and three pools

children.text: The beach in front of the resort is a white-sand stretch about

long. On days when you would rather skip the sea, you can use three swimming pools of different sizes and depths. A children's pool and a water slide are also reported, which makes the resort easy for families.

Kayaking, paddleboarding, jet skis and parasailing are listed as activities. Snorkeling and PADI Discover Scuba Diving are also offered, so you can get a light taste of the underwater world without a diving certificate. Activities and prices depend on the weather and operating conditions.

This is the land activity area built around the forested terrain. Horseback riding, ATVs, ziplining, hiking and rock climbing are listed. Advance sign-up and safety-gear rules may apply, so ask at the front desk first thing about what is available today.
The golf course is described as a 50-hectare, 18-hole layout, par 72 and about
6,500 yards
long, with views over the Sulu Sea. If you travel with non-golfers, they can spend the time at the beach and pools while you play.

This upscale annex sits on a rocky hill. It is known for king beds, jacuzzis, rain showers and an infinity pool, and guests travel to and from the main resort by van. It is popular for honeymoons and anniversaries, so book early in peak season.

Listed venues include Bamboo Garden for Filipino food by the beach, Il Patio Ristorante for Italian, Sea Catch for seafood, and the beachside Tiki Bar. The lineup can change, so check the current list of open outlets when you arrive.

blocks.title: A day trip to Rizal's exile sites

children.text: The drive from the resort to Rizal Park is listed at around
10 minutes
. There you will find restored huts, the dam and aqueduct Rizal built, the Rizaliana Museum and more, so you can add a history outing to a beach holiday.
The resort also describes a yoga wellness club. Some travelers start the day with an early yoga class and a walk on the beach. Check class times and fees when you book.

items.title: Day visit
items.subtitle: Enjoy the beach on a day tour

children.text: Leave from Dipolog Airport or Dapitan town and arrive at the resort. If you are a day-tour guest, first confirm at the entrance how the visit works and what is included.
Spend the early hours at the beach and pools. The sun is gentler in the morning and the sea is relatively calm.
Have lunch at a resort restaurant. Visitor accounts from 2018 and 2023 reported a day-tour fee of
as a pass usable for food and activities; please confirm on site whether that still applies.
Pick one light water activity, such as kayaking or paddleboarding. Activities may cost extra.
Shower and head back to Dapitan. If you leave before sunset, you can stop at the town waterfront promenade or the Rizal landing site to round out the day.
The day-tour arrangement and fee come from 2018 and 2023 visitor accounts (both ₱1,000) and may differ now. Before you go, ask the resort directly whether it is available and what today's fee is.

items.title: 2 days, 1 night
items.subtitle: Relax and see Rizal sites together

children.text: Land at Dipolog Airport and transfer to the resort by resort shuttle or taxi. The transfer takes about
30–45 minutes
Check-in starts at 15:00, so eat lunch first and leave your bags at the front desk. After check-in, spend the first afternoon swimming at the beach.
Have dinner at a resort restaurant and a drink at a beach bar.
After breakfast, pick one water sport or safari zone activity. If you signed up for yoga, this is a good time.
Check-out is before 12:00. Pack up, leave the resort and head to Rizal Park.
Have lunch near the Rizal Shrine, walk around the historic sites in Dapitan town, then continue to the airport or the port.
Work backward from your flight time and aim to be at the airport 2 hours before departure. The distance from Dapitan to the airport is about
14 km
Cebu Pacific and PAL Express are reported to fly nonstop from Manila (MNL) to Dipolog Airport (DPL), with a flight time of about
1 hour 35 minutes–1 hour 45 minutes
From Cebu, Cebgo serves Dipolog Airport. Schedules and fares change with the season, so check the airline's official app for the latest times.
From Dipolog Airport to the resort is about
30–45 minutes
by car. A resort shuttle pickup is listed, so ask when booking whether you can arrange it and what it costs.
To reach Dapitan town from the airport, you can also take a tricycle from the airport to the Dipolog town terminal and then transfer to a van or minibus.
Fast crafts and ferries from several operators run between Dumaguete port and Dapitan port. The crossing time varies by source, from about
3–4 hours
Fares are listed at roughly
depending on the operator and seat class. Schedules change often, so confirm with the operator before boarding.
From Dapitan port, take a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) or a tricycle to the resort.

items.title: From Dapitan town to the resort

children.text: From Dapitan town to the resort is about
5 km
along the coastal road.
Visitor accounts from 2018 and 2023 put a motorcycle taxi at about
and a tricycle at about
(tricycle figure from 2012 and 2018 posts; some quotes include a round trip with waiting). Agree on the current fare before you ride.
A rental car or hotel pickup makes things easier for families with lots of luggage.
Buses run from Cagayan de Oro to Dipolog. A 2018 account put the ride at about
9 hours
and around
, but this is a single source I could not confirm elsewhere, so treat it as a rough guide only.
From Dipolog to Dapitan is about
14 km
, served by vans and minibuses.
If you are building the trip around beach activities, pick a time with little rain and calm seas. Philippine beaches are generally best in the dry season,
December–May
, but monthly weather in Zamboanga del Norte varies from year to year, so check the forecast just before you leave.
The resort gets busy on weekends and holidays. In peak season, rooms and water activities can fill up early, so a weekday stay is recommended if possible.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The New Year and Christmas holidays are crowded and rates may rise. Book early.
The best time for water sports and beach swimming. Sun protection is essential.
Sea activities can be canceled, so check the weather. Ask whether any promotions are running.

Room types listed include Deluxe, Prime, Garden and Family Pavilion. The Deluxe room has one king bed or two queen beds, suiting business travelers and small families, while the Family room has multiple beds and two bathrooms for larger groups. Premium rooms and villas cost much more, so choose within your budget.

Most meals are taken at the resort's own restaurants. Filipino home cooking, Italian, seafood and beach bars are listed, and some reviews say prices are high. To save money, you can eat at restaurants in Dapitan town; weigh the travel time and transport costs against the savings.
Confirm available facilities and rates directly with the resort before booking. The owner changed in May 2026, so operations may have changed.
Check-in starts at 15:00 and check-out is before 12:00. If you arrive early, you can leave your bags and relax on the beach first.
Arrange an airport pickup in advance, timed to your flight arrival.
It is safest to sign up for water sports and safari activities a day ahead. They can be canceled for weather or safety reasons.
The grounds are fairly large on foot. At check-in, ask about golf carts or the shuttle.
Rizal Park is listed as open from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Some sources say Tuesday to Sunday, so it may be closed on Mondays.
You will need cash pesos outside the resort. Withdraw some in advance from an ATM in Dapitan town.
Bring sunscreen, a hat and mosquito repellent.

In March 2025 the Supreme Court ordered the resort's operating company to return a 1,602-square-meter lot it had leased. Ownership changed in May 2026, so confirm the operating status and what is available before booking.
Prices vary widely between travel sites and visitor accounts, and many figures are old. Check the official information and the refund policy before you pay.
Water activities can be halted depending on sea conditions. Always wear a life jacket and follow staff instructions.
Mosquitoes and insects can be plentiful on the beach and forested hillside. Wear long sleeves or repellent around dusk.
Flights into Dipolog Airport are not frequent, so a cancellation or delay can upset your plans. Leave plenty of margin for your departure flight.
Agree on the fare before you take a rental car or taxi, and avoid traveling at night.
About
10 minutes
by car from the resort. It has restored huts where José Rizal lived during his exile, a dam and a museum. It was declared a national shrine in 1973.
This stretch of the Dapitan waterfront, about
4.9 km
from the resort, is known as the place where Rizal came ashore. It is close to the town center, so it pairs well with a walk around town.
A church built in 1871 in Dapitan town, about
5.4 km
from the resort. It is a good stop during a stroll through town.
About
14 km
from Dapitan, this is the main city of Zamboanga del Norte. It has the airport and terminals, making it the gateway for getting around.
